answers.note: Thorough, well-sequenced plan with separate pre-meetings, clear ground rules, full restorative question set, a signed agreement and two-stage follow-up, though parents are not mentioned.
Sound restorative questions and repair ideas, but the joint meeting is thin and has no ground rules, and it invents a teacher failing ('I should have checked in on Monday').
Complete and practical plan covering willingness checks, ground rules, restorative questions, written repair agreement, parent messages, safeguarding and one-week follow-up.
Strong coaching flow with a live recall experiment that shows her why retrieval beats rereading, but the target is set for one week not a fortnight and the follow-up has no date or measure.

Well-timed and student-led, but it deliberately avoids explaining why active methods beat rereading and the goal-setting questions come after the action, with a one-week rather than fortnightly target.

Detailed, coaching-led session with a blank-page recall demo, specific when/where action, confidence check, record template and next-session preview, though the target covers a week rather than a fortnight.
Covers all three themes with varied, practical daily activities, but sessions have no minute-by-minute timings, several look overloaded for 15 minutes, and scenario cards must be made by the tutor.

Consistent 15-minute routine with timed sessions for weeks 1 to 2, practical habits (night-before bag routine, planner, charging outside bedroom) and belonging-building compliment cards, though weeks 3 to 4 are only outlined.
A generic reading/current events/careers template that drifts off the three requested themes, gives phones only thin coverage and requires the tutor to source many reading extracts and news stories.
